q: When water is released immediately from the main, what system can be used to supply higher levels?
n: A deluge system is supplied through a valve that releases water immediately from the main to all open heads, delivering large flows to the protected levels. Source: NFPA 13 / NFPA 15.

q: What pipe supplies each floor with water for firefighting?
n: A standpipe is the vertical fire water pipe with hose valves at each floor, so firefighters can connect hoses on every level. Source: NFPA 14; RA 9514 Fire Code RIRR 2019.

q: What is the maximum height of a Siamese connection from the ground line?
n: Fire department (Siamese) connections are installed between about 450 mm and 1,200 mm above grade, so the 1,200 mm figure is the maximum height. Source: NFPA 14 (fire department connections); RA 9514 Fire Code RIRR 2019.

q: What is a Siamese (fire department) connection for?
o: Letting fire trucks pump water into the standpipe or sprinkler system
n: A Siamese connection lets fire trucks pump water into the building's standpipe or sprinkler system to boost its supply and pressure. Source: NFPA 13/14; RA 9514 Fire Code RIRR 2019.

q: Which system is set off by heat and discharges only at the heads that open?
n: In a wet-pipe system water is already at every head, and only the heads whose bulbs or links are fused by the heat open and discharge. Source: NFPA 13.

q: Which pump is used to eject sewage or liquid waste?
n: A sump pump of the ejector type lifts sewage or liquid waste from fixtures below the sewer level up to the building drain or sewer. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (sumps and ejectors).

q: Which pump removes water from the lowest part of a building?
n: A sump pump removes water collected in a pit at the lowest part of a building, such as a basement or elevator pit. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (sumps).

q: What is the best location for installing a water pump?
n: The water pump is installed at the cistern, the storage it draws from, so its suction line is short and it is easy to prime. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (water supply); ASPE Plumbing Engineering Design Handbook.

q: Where is a pump ideally located in relation to a cistern?
o: Side by side with the cistern
n: Setting the pump on top of the cistern keeps the suction line short and vertical and the pump dry, with easy access for maintenance. Source: Philippine plumbing practice; ASPE Plumbing Engineering Design Handbook.

q: Which pump keeps adequate pressure on the upper floors of a multi-story building?
n: A booster pump raises pressure so upper floors still get adequate pressure despite the static head lost with height. Source: ASPE Plumbing Engineering Design Handbook; National Plumbing Code of the Philippines.

q: Considering the operational needs and potential emergency scenarios in a three-storey hospital, how many elevators are recommended to serve both patients and staff?
o: One, but it is ideal to have one for passengers
One for passengers and one for patients on stretchers
n: A small hospital should have at least one passenger elevator and one stretcher (bed) elevator, so patients on stretchers can be moved even when the other lift is busy or out of service. Source: DOH Planning and Design Guidelines for Hospitals; Time-Saver Standards (hospitals).

q: Given the building height and expected load of a three-storey hospital, which type of elevator system is most appropriate for efficient and safe vertical transportation?
n: For a three-storey hospital either a traction or a hydraulic elevator is appropriate, both safe and efficient at low rise. Source: Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook; DOH hospital design guidelines.

q: In the design of a three-storey hospital, which of the following fire suppression systems is typically NOT included in standard fire safety protocols?
n: A dry standpipe is typically not part of a three-storey hospital's fire protection: dry standpipes are required only in taller buildings, while extinguishers, wet standpipes and sprinklers are. Source: RA 9514 Fire Code RIRR 2019 (standpipe requirements).

q: According to fire code requirements, how many dry standpipes are typically required in a three-storey hospital?
n: The Fire Code requires dry standpipes only in buildings four storeys or more, so a three-storey hospital needs none. Source: RA 9514 Fire Code RIRR 2019 (standpipe systems).

q: What is the most appropriate and code-compliant location for installing a dry standpipe in a hospital?
n: Standpipe outlets are placed in the enclosed exit stairways, where firefighters stage and attack the fire from a protected area. Source: NFPA 14; RA 9514 Fire Code RIRR 2019.

q: Which of these does NOT make elevators?
o: None of the above — all three do
n: Hyundai, Mitsubishi and Hitachi all make elevators, so the answer is none of the above. Source: Hyundai Elevator, Mitsubishi Electric and Hitachi company websites.

q: Which brand is well known for its ultra-fast elevators used in skyscrapers?
n: Mitsubishi Electric is known for ultra-fast elevators, including some of the world's fastest in Shanghai Tower. Source: Mitsubishi Electric company press releases.

q: Which elevator brand is from Finland?
n: KONE Corporation is headquartered in Espoo, Finland. KONE is one of the world's largest elevator and escalator makers, alongside Otis (USA), Schindler (Switzerland) and Mitsubishi (Japan). Source: KONE company website.

q: Which is one of the oldest elevator makers, founded in the United States?
n: Otis is one of the oldest elevator makers, founded in the United States. Elisha Otis demonstrated his safety brake in 1854. Source: Otis company history.

q: Which German company makes elevators and escalators worldwide?
n: Thyssenkrupp (now TK Elevator) is the German maker. Schindler is Swiss and KONE is Finnish. Source: TK Elevator company website.

q: Which of these makes elevators and escalators?
n: KONE makes elevators and escalators. Honeywell and Bosch make building controls and appliances. Source: KONE company website.

q: After how many minutes of inactivity will an escalator temporarily stop to save electricity?
n: Escalators with auto-stop or standby mode typically pause or slow after about three minutes with no passengers, saving energy. Source: Escalator manufacturer literature (KONE, Schindler).

q: What is the minimum load capacity of a home elevator in kilograms?
n: Home (residential) elevators are commonly rated for a minimum of about 250 kg. Source: ASME A17.1 Sec. 5.3 (private residence elevators); manufacturer literature.

q: What do you call the door inside the elevator?
n: The door on the elevator car itself is the cab (car) door. The hoistway door is at each landing. Source: ASME A17.1; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook.

q: Which part opens and closes elevator doors automatically?
n: The door operator, a motor drive on the car top, opens and closes the car door and couples to the landing door. Source: ASME A17.1; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook.

q: Which is NOT a fire protection device?
n: A firewall is a fire-rated building element that limits spread, not a fire protection device. Smoke detectors, helmets and sprinklers are devices and equipment. Source: RA 9514 Fire Code RIRR 2019 (definitions).

q: What device senses smoke and triggers an alarm?
n: A smoke detector senses smoke particles (ionization or photoelectric) and triggers the alarm. Source: NFPA 72.

q: Which part discharges water automatically when it senses heat?
n: A sprinkler head opens automatically when heat breaks its glass bulb or melts its fusible link, discharging water on the fire. Source: NFPA 13.

q: Which equipment is used to put out small fires by hand?
n: A portable fire extinguisher is used by hand to put out small, incipient fires. Source: NFPA 10; RA 9514 Fire Code RIRR 2019.
